title: When 1+1 $\neq$ 2: Benchmarking Civil-Time Reasoning in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.29972v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Calendar arithmetic is non-linear. When 1:59 AM + 1 minute occurs during daylight saving spring-forward, the result is 3:00 AM, not 2:00 AM, as the hour is skipped. We introduce CivilTime-Bench, a benchmark for civil-time reasoning covering daylight saving transitions, non-hour offsets, date-line crossings, and ISO week boundaries. With 60,011 training and 10,500 evaluation examples under strict output-contract evaluation, we benchmark seven LLMs (six instruction-tuned models and Llama-3.1-8B base) and find: zero-shot exact match varies substantially across models, contract-aware prompting often improves format compliance but yields inconsistent accuracy gains, few-shot in-context learning provides model-dependent improvements, and fine-tuning achieves 74.6--86.6% EM on synthetic evaluation but only 36.6--45.2% on HumanTime-500 for models with valid results on both splits, highlighting substantial limitations in generalization. translated_title: 当1+1≠2：大语言模型民用时间推理的基准测试
translated_abstract: 日历算术是非线性的。当凌晨1:59加1分钟发生在夏令时春季时钟拨快期间时，结果是3:00 AM而非2:00 AM，因为该小时被跳过了。我们提出了CivilTime-Bench，一个民用时间推理基准，涵盖夏令时转换、非整小时偏移、日界线跨越和ISO周边界。在严格的输出契约评估下，基于60,011个训练样本和10,500个评估样本，我们对七个大语言模型（六个指令微调模型和Llama-3.1-8B基础模型）进行了基准测试，发现：零样本精确匹配率在不同模型之间差异显著；契约感知提示通常能改善格式合规性，但带来的准确率提升并不一致；少样本上下文学习的改进因模型而异；微调在合成评估上达到74.6–86.6%的精确匹配率，但在两个数据集上均有有效结果的模型在HumanTime-500上仅达到36.6–45.2%，凸显了泛化能力的重大局限。我们公开发布……（原文摘要末尾被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出CivilTime-Bench基准，系统评估大语言模型在夏令时转换等非线性民用时间（日历）推理上的能力，发现即使借助契约感知提示、少样本学习或微调，模型在真实场景中的准确率与泛化能力仍存在显著局限。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces CivilTime-Bench, a benchmark for non-linear civil-time reasoning (e.g., DST transitions, date-line crossings), showing that LLMs—despite contract-aware prompting, few-shot learning, or fine-tuning—still exhibit substantial accuracy gaps and poor generalization on real-world evaluation.
